newsitem.title: USA: Unison HealthCare bonds continue decline.
newsitem.headline: Unison HealthCare bonds continue decline.

text.p: Unison HealthCare Corp bonds continued a selloff begun earlier in the week after the company said pretax losses would exceed forecasts.
On Monday, the company said the pretax loss for that period would be "significantly higher" than the $5 million to $6 million loss previously estimated, triggering a sellof in the bonds.
"Unison's bonds fell seven points since news hit the wire of potentially higher-than-expected pretax losses," said one trader of distressed debt.

Unison, a long-term and specialty care health services provider, announced in March it would restate its financial results for the nine months ended September 30, 1996, due to accounting inaccurancies.
Unison 12-1/4 bonds due 2006 which began the week quoted at 82 bid, 86 offer, were quoted Wednesday afternoon at 75 bid, 80 offer, traders said.
The company was not immediately available for comment.
In an earlier release, the company said it expects to report audited financial statements for 1996 within the next two weeks.
Unison is facing legal challenges from an investor who has accused Unison, its officers and directors of omitting material facts about its performance.
In March, the company said it hired a law firm to conduct a special review of the facts and circumstances surrounding the restatement.
In addition, Unison said recent lawsuits relating to the decline in the company's stock price would be vigorously defended.
Unison stock was trading at 2-3/8 on Wednesday, unchanged from Tuesday's close, while having reached a 52 week high of 15-1/2 and a low of 1-7/8.
Unison's senior unsecured debt is rated single-B by Standard & Poor's and Caa by Moody's Investors Service Inc. Both rating agencies have placed Unison under review for potential downgrade.
